subject: Error: station directory was not found in digiKam albums.

messages.author: 39547915185f5c9f
messages.subject: Error: station directory was not found in digiKam albums.
parts:
Hello camtrapR team,

I am planning on working with video data am trying to run your vignettes on some pilot data. I'm stuck at the following point and your help would be very much appreciated:

I am trying to construct the recordTable like this:

table <- recordTable("renamedImages", IDfrom = "metadata", timeZone ="America/Cayenne",  metadataSpeciesTag = "Species",
                     video=list(file_formats=c("mp4"), dateTimeTag="QuickTime:CreateDate",
                                db_directory=getwd(), db_filename="digikam4.db"))

But I get the following error: "Error: station directory renamedImages/StationA/ was not found in digiKam albums. Skipping"

My digiCam looks like the attached screenshot if it helps. Please let me know if you need any other information. Many thanks!

Kind regards, 

Yannick Wiegers

messages.author: 39547915185f5c9f
messages.subject: Re: Error: station directory was not found in digiKam albums.
parts:
After some more troubleshooting of my own I think I've found the issue:

It's this line in the 'digiKamVideoHierarchicalSubject' function:

if (!stationDir %in% paste(Albums[, pathColumn],collapse="")) {

 I think the %in% (from data.table I think?) doesn't work or something?

Doing the same thing but with grepl has fixed this:

  if(sum((grepl(pattern=stationDir,x=Albums[, pathColumn])))==0){

Any feedback on whether this is correct is appreciated!

Cheers, 

Yannick

messages.author: 39547915185f5c9f
messages.subject: Re: Error: station directory was not found in digiKam albums.
parts:
If someone ever has the same problem, I think it was due to file paths being incorrectly matched to one another for some reason. I think I solved it for my case by changing two things:

In the function 'digiKamVideoHierarchicalSubject':

pathColumn <- "albumPath_full2"
    if (!stationDir %in% Albums[, pathColumn]) {


TO:

 pathColumn <- "albumPath_full2"  
   Albums$albumPath_full2 <- paste(Albums$label,Albums$relativePath,sep="")
  if (!stationDir0 %in% Albums[, pathColumn]) {

And in 'addVideoHierarchicalSubject' I changed

metadata.tmp.video$HierarchicalSubject_video <- digiKamVideoMetadata$HierarchicalSubject[match(metadata.tmp.almostFullPath,
        digiKamVideoMetadata$almostFullPath)]

TO:


metadata.tmp.video$HierarchicalSubject_video <- digiKamVideoMetadata$HierarchicalSubject[match(digiKamVideoMetadata$name,
                                                                metadata.tmp.video$FileName)]


Not sure why the normal functions didn't find matches as the file paths looked very similar. But in any case, it works now.

Cheers, 

Yannick

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Re: Error: station directory was not found in digiKam albums.
parts:
Hi Yannick,

I am concerned about the way you specified inDir in your original code:

recordTable("renamedImages", ...

I would always specify full paths, and not rely on the working directory being set correctly in order to make the function work. The error message in the first post:
"Error: station directory renamedImages/StationA/ was not found in digiKam albums. Skipping"

suggests that the function can't match the station name (or rather, the station name you provided does not match the full path name stored in the digiKam data base). Instead of "renamedImages/StationA/" it should be a full path. See the examples in this thread:

https://groups.google.com/g/camtrapr/c/rW2rtWHU-ts

Try replacing inDir with the full path and let us know if the error persists (with the native camtrapR functions, not your adapted version).

Best regards,

Jürgen

If someone ever has the same problem, I think it was due to file paths being incorrectly matched to one another for some reason. I think I solved it for my case by changing two things:

In the function 'digiKamVideoHierarchicalSubject':

pathColumn <- "albumPath_full2"
    if (!stationDir %in% Albums[, pathColumn]) {


TO:

 pathColumn <- "albumPath_full2"  
   Albums$albumPath_full2 <- paste(Albums$label,Albums$relativePath,sep="")
  if (!stationDir0 %in% Albums[, pathColumn]) {

And in 'addVideoHierarchicalSubject' I changed

metadata.tmp.video$HierarchicalSubject_video <- digiKamVideoMetadata$HierarchicalSubject[match(metadata.tmp.almostFullPath,
        digiKamVideoMetadata$almostFullPath)]

TO:


metadata.tmp.video$HierarchicalSubject_video <- digiKamVideoMetadata$HierarchicalSubject[match(digiKamVideoMetadata$name,
                                                                metadata.tmp.video$FileName)]


Not sure why the normal functions didn't find matches as the file paths looked very similar. But in any case, it works now.

Cheers, 

Yannick
